PrinterStatus.description:
Printer status sourced from the printer_status_cache table.

The endpoint reads the cache row written by StatusProbeProducer instead
of doing a synchronous SNMP probe inline.  This makes the response fast
(<10 ms) even when the printer is offline.

``tape_loaded`` is a human-readable string such as
``"12mm laminated black/clear"`` or ``None`` when no tape is inserted.
``error_state`` mirrors the active PrinterError flags as a string, or
``None`` when the printer is ready.
``captured_at`` is the UTC timestamp of the probe that last updated the
cache row.  ``None`` means no probe has completed yet.  For a page printer
(``kind="page"``) that went offline it stays the time of the last
*successful* reading; ``online`` and ``last_error`` tell that it is stale.
``last_probe_age_s`` is the age of the cached reading in seconds (for an
offline page printer: since its last successful reading).
``last_error`` is the exception message from the most recent failed probe.
``note`` carries a human-readable hint (e.g. "No probe yet").
``polled`` is ``False`` when no status producer runs for the printer (SNMP discovery
off, printer disabled or not wired). ``stale`` is ``True`` when the last probe attempt
(``printer_status_cache.updated_at``) is older than
``max(90, 3 * probe interval, 2 * max backoff)`` seconds (an IPP printer that stopped answering
is probed with a backoff of up to 300 s, so its bound is 600 s),
or implausibly in the future. For an unpolled or stale printer ``online`` is
``None`` and the cached values (tape, error state, markers, trays) are not returned;
``captured_at`` and ``last_probe_age_s`` stay so a client can show how old the last
reading is.

Subsequent GETs return only the prefix. A key with the admin scope always acts on every printer: a non-empty ``allowed_printer_ids`` on it is 422 ``admin_key_not_restrictable``.

post.description: Legt einen neuen Drucker an. Slug und Name müssen eindeutig sein. Gibt 409 zurück wenn Slug oder Name bereits vergeben ist. An ``ipp`` printer is probed first; nothing is saved when it is unreachable (409 ``ipp_unreachable``), accepts no PDF (409 ``ipp_pdf_unsupported``) or does not report a configured tray (422 ``tray_unknown``). The printer is wired into the running hub before the answer; no restart is needed.
post.summary: Neuen Drucker anlegen

post.description: Runs Get-Printer-Attributes against the given URI now and returns a bounded summary (make and model, IPP and PDF versions, resolutions, media, trays, colour modes, margins, state); never the raw attributes. Errors: 502 ``ipp_unreachable``, ``ipp_rejected`` (IPP status name in ``error_detail``) or ``ipp_bad_response``. Admin only.
post.summary: Read an IPP printer

post.description: Ends the device-swap flag of a printer (#231). ``same_device`` accepts the flagged device as the printer and keeps its calibration; ``replaced`` does the same and deletes every stored calibration of the printer, in one transaction. The held sheet and calibration jobs are released once the change is committed. 404 for an unknown printer, 409 ``no-identity-mismatch`` when no swap is flagged and 409 ``identity-changed`` when the flagged device is no longer the one reviewed. Admin only.
post.summary: Resolve a flagged device swap

get.description: Gibt einen Drucker per Slug zurück. 404 wenn kein Drucker mit diesem Slug existiert.

put.description: Aktualisiert einen Drucker per PATCH-Semantik (nur geänderte Felder). Slug und ID können nicht geändert werden. Gibt 404 zurück wenn kein Drucker mit diesem Slug existiert. ``connection`` must fit the stored backend (422 ``invalid_connection``); ``trays`` (replace-all) are for ``ipp`` printers only (422 ``trays_not_allowed``). ``connection.snmp.community`` is write-only: omitted or null keeps the stored one while host and port stay the same; a new host or port without a community, or discovery without any community, is 422 ``snmp_community_required``. An ``ipp`` printer is probed again when its URI changes or a tray key is new. A change of the connection, the trays or the IPP queue timeout re-wires the printer before the answer: a job printing on it finishes first (up to its queue timeout), waiting jobs stay queued. A rename re-wires nothing.

post.description: Deaktiviert einen Drucker (Soft-Delete). Gibt 404 zurück wenn kein Drucker mit diesem Slug existiert. Gibt 409 zurück wenn der Drucker bereits deaktiviert ist. Takes effect before the answer: polling stops and new jobs are refused (409 ``printer-unavailable``); a job printing on it finishes first (up to its queue timeout), waiting jobs stay queued and print after enable.
post.summary: Drucker deaktivieren

post.description: Aktiviert einen deaktivierten Drucker. Gibt 404 zurück wenn kein Drucker mit diesem Slug existiert. Gibt 409 zurück wenn der Drucker bereits aktiv ist. The printer is wired again before the answer; no restart is needed.
post.summary: Drucker aktivieren

Live-Updates. ``run`` shows a tape run that prints, waits for a
confirmation, or stopped (#277).

post.description: A tape batch of more than 50 labels prints in sub-jobs; each further sub-job starts only after this call, for example after the user checked or changed the tape (#277). Held runs live in memory: a hub restart fails every label that waited for a confirmation (`tape_run_interrupted`), also a part that was continued but had not started, and a stopped run can then no longer be reprinted (`run` is `null`, this answers 404). A held run counts against `LABELYARD_MAX_QUEUED_RUNS_PER_KEY` (default 20) of its key, not against the printer's cap: over it a new batch of that key answers 429 `too-many-queued-runs` until a run is continued, reprinted to the end or discarded. At most five runs per printer are held, at most two of one key: a further held run discards that key's own oldest (`run_discarded_limit`), never another key's. While the five places are taken, a batch of more than 50 labels from a key without a held run there gets 429 `too-many-queued-runs`; smaller batches are always taken. All callers without a key (SSO users) count as one key; a browser session signed in with a key counts as that key.

403.description: The key lacks the `print` scope or may not use this printer.

404.description: No such batch, or no tape run of it that waits for an action.

409.description: The run is in another state (`run_not_awaiting_confirmation`, `run_not_stopped`, `run_not_held`), or a run that waited 15 minutes and gave up its pictures cannot draw them again from the stored labels (`run_pictures_lost`; discard it).

post.description: A stopped run (#277): with `stop_kind` `unknown` the group's outcome is unknown — count what printed, fix the tape, and reprint from the first label that is missing (`reprint_from` to `reprint_to`); that label to the end of the group, and every label that was not started, are queued again as new jobs, and the labels before it count as printed. With `refused` nothing of the group was sent: reprint from its first label. A printer the stop paused is resumed. Labels whose stored job was cleaned up are listed in `skipped_job_ids`. The batch then lists the run's labels (`GET` shows the new jobs). `from_label` outside the range answers 422 `label_out_of_range`. get.description: Return the full job record for the given UUID.  Returns 404 if not found; for an API key without ``admin`` scope also for a job another key (or a browser, SSO user or webhook) submitted.  Cancel, retry, pause and resume answer the same 404.

post.description: Cancels a job that is in ``queued`` state.  Returns 409 ProblemDetail when the job is in ``printing`` (or any other non-QUEUED) state — mid-print abort is unsafe over TCP/9100 because the raster data is already on the wire.  Exception: a page job (IPP printer) that the printer already holds is cancelled at the printer: the hub sends Cancel-Job and answers ``202`` with the job still ``printing``; the job ends ``cancelled`` (or ``failed``/``interrupted`` when the page had started) once the printer confirms.

202.description: Cancel requested at the printer (page job)

post.summary: Cancel a queued job

post.description: Placeholder — returns 501 ProblemDetail.  Mid-job pause will be implemented when the queue worker gains control-plane support for pausing an in-progress raster stream.  This endpoint exists so the Phase 7 UI can wire to a stable URL.
post.summary: Pause a job (not yet implemented)

post.description: Placeholder — returns 501 ProblemDetail.  Resume will be implemented alongside pause in a later phase.  This endpoint exists so the Phase 7 UI can wire to a stable URL.
post.summary: Resume a paused job (not yet implemented)

post.description: Clones a ``failed`` (or ``failed_restart`` / ``cancelled``) job into a new ``queued`` job with a fresh UUID.  The original job is untouched and remains as an immutable history entry.  The new job is handed to the print queue immediately — no restart needed.  Returns 409 when the original job is still in an active state (``queued`` or ``printing``) or its printer is not available, and 422 when the stored payload cannot be re-rendered (e.g. webhook-created jobs).  A Grocy label job that failed before its render (printer offline, no tape) is accepted again on its printer and completes in the background, like the webhook; a Grocy label that could not be built answers 422 and creates no row.  Page jobs: a calibration page is re-submitted from its payload, so retry prints the same page again with its original calibration snapshot and date; a fresh check print with the current calibration is a new calibration-page request.  A sheet page is retried onto the same cells of the same sheet as a new job, with a fresh calibration snapshot and the margin ID and feed mark decided again for the printer.  It answers 409 ``job_not_retryable`` for a ``done`` job (or an ID-only job whose ID was printed since), 409 ``cells_unconfirmed`` while a cell of the job waits for confirmation, 409 ``cells_taken`` (with the cell numbers) when a cell is no longer free, 409 ``printer_disabled`` for a disabled printer (a calibration page too), 422 ``tray_unknown`` when the tray was removed or disabled since, and 409 ``sheet_discarded`` for a discarded sheet; nothing is reserved or created in any of these cases.
post.summary: Retry a failed job

get.description: Looks up an entity from the given integration app by its identifier.  ``app`` must be one of ``snipeit``, ``grocy``, or ``spoolman`` — an unsupported value returns 422.  Returns 404 ProblemDetail when the entity does not exist in the integration's backend.  The ``url`` field is the deep-link to the entity in the integration's own web UI, suitable for embedding in a QR code or label.

post.description: Submit a label-print job.  The job is queued and dispatched asynchronously by the queue worker.  Returns 202 with the new job's UUID and state ``queued``.  Returns 4xx/5xx on printer errors (tape mismatch, offline, cover open, etc.).
post.summary: Submit a print job

post.description: Validates all items and enqueues the batch as one tape run — no per-item errors are returned. The labels (copies included) print in sub-jobs of at most 50; each further sub-job waits for `POST /api/v1/batches/{batch_id}/continue`. Inside a sub-job the labels go out in groups of 10 with a status check after each; when a group fails, the run stops (see `GET /api/v1/batches/{batch_id}`). A tape end stops it when the printer reports it: a PT sets the SNMP `noPaper` bit; whether a QL-820NWB reports the end of a DK roll is not verified, so on a QL the check reliably catches only an unreachable printer and an open cover. Any validation failure or hardware precondition (printer_offline, cover_open, unsupported_tape, no_tape_loaded, content_type_data_mismatch) rejects the whole batch with the appropriate 4xx status code. A page printer (IPP) answers 409 media_kind_mismatch. A printer holds at most `LABELYARD_MAX_QUEUED_RUNS_PER_PRINTER` (default 5) runs and a key at most `LABELYARD_MAX_QUEUED_RUNS_PER_KEY` (default 20); a run counts until it is over. A run that waits for `/continue` or a reprint counts against its key only. Over a cap the batch answers 429 too-many-queued-runs.
post.summary: Submit a batch of print jobs

post.description: Reserves the cells for the items and queues one page job per planned page; the cells turn `used` when a page has printed. Send the preview's `expected_cells` to be refused (`plan_changed`) if the plan moved since. Nothing is reserved if an item fails: a lookup, or a cell that cannot show the item (the error names `item_index`). A sheet job has no copies. One run prints one sheet: the first items as many as it takes; the response says how many were placed and how many remain (`placed`, `remaining`). The response names the job of each page, where its sheet ID and feed-direction mark are printed, and one batch id for all of them.

403.description: The key lacks the `print` scope, or may not use this printer (`printer_not_allowed`).

404.description: Unknown printer (`printer_not_found`), sheet (`sheet_not_found`), sheet type, or an item the integration does not have (`app-lookup-not-found`).

409.description: Not a page printer (`media_kind_mismatch`), the printer is disabled (`printer_disabled`) or unknown to the print queue (`printer-unavailable`), the device behind the printer changed (`printer-identity-mismatch`), the sheet is discarded or archived, the cells do not fit (`insufficient_cells`, `cells_taken`), or the plan differs from `expected_cells` (`plan_changed`, with the new plan).

422.description: Invalid request (`invalid_request`, field paths only), an unknown or disabled tray (`tray_unknown`), an item the cell cannot show (`content_type_data_mismatch`), or an unknown integration (`integration_unknown_app`). Item errors carry `item_index`.

502.description: An integration lookup failed (`integration_lookup_failed`), or the print stopped after some pages were queued (`print_interrupted`, or the error of that page with `batch_id` and `job_ids` in `error_detail`: those pages keep printing).

post.summary: Print labels onto sheets

post.description: Plans where the items would go and draws them, without reserving or printing anything. Per page: every cell with its state, a 150 dpi PNG of the new content only, whether the sheet ID and the feed-direction mark are printed, and where. Also the cells left free, the plan to send back as `expected_cells`, and where lookup items were printed before. The picture is never calibrated. Only page (IPP) printers print sheets. A run plans one sheet: a second placement is refused (`preview_too_large`), and the items the sheet does not take are left out (`placed`, `remaining`).

403.description: These credentials may not use this printer (`printer_not_allowed`).

404.description: Unknown printer (`printer_not_found`), sheet (`sheet_not_found`), sheet type, or an item the integration does not have (`app-lookup-not-found`).

409.description: Not a page printer (`media_kind_mismatch`), the printer is disabled (`printer_disabled`), the sheet is discarded or archived, or the cells do not fit (`insufficient_cells`, `cells_taken`).

422.description: Invalid request (`invalid_request`, field paths only), an unknown or disabled tray (`tray_unknown`), an item the cell cannot show (`content_type_data_mismatch`), a plan of more than one sheet (`preview_too_large`), or an unknown integration (`integration_unknown_app`). Item errors carry `item_index`.

429.description: The key has a preview in progress already, or a render of the key is stuck past the time limit (`too-many-previews`): one per key at a time. The body has the rate limit's shape (`retry_after_seconds`).

503.description: An integration is not configured (`integration_not_configured`), or no render slot became free in time (`render-unavailable`): every slot is held by a stuck render, the callers without a key have a stuck render, or the wait for the caller's turn (one slot per key, one for all callers without a key) reached `LABELYARD_RENDER_TIMEOUT_S`.

504.description: A page took longer than `LABELYARD_RENDER_TIMEOUT_S` to draw (`render-timeout`). The drawing goes on: the key's next preview answers 429 `too-many-previews` until it has ended.

post.summary: Preview a sheet print

A tape width without a geometry entry also gives ``media`` null. A stale reading or an unpolled printer is reported as unknown too (``media`` null, ``stale`` true, ``captured_at`` kept). post.description: Bulk-cancels every job in ``queued`` state for this printer, including jobs that are waiting while the printer is paused; none of them is sent to the printer.  Jobs in ``printing`` state are intentionally **not** cancelled — a mid-print abort is unsafe over TCP/9100 because the raster data is already on the wire; a page job the IPP printer already holds is left to finish as well (cancel it with ``POST /api/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel``).  An API key without ``admin`` scope cancels only the queued jobs it submitted; the jobs of other keys and of browser or SSO users stay queued.  Returns 204 even when there are no queued jobs.
post.summary: Cancel all queued jobs for a printer

post.description: Sets ``printer_state.paused = false`` and releases the queue worker, including an automatic pause after a printer error.  Idempotent — resuming an already-active printer returns 204 without error.
post.summary: Resume job dispatch for a printer

get.description: Returns the roll identity last seen by the status probe, the tape colour the operator gave it and whether the operator is still to be asked. All fields are empty until the first probe. Answers 404 for an unknown printer.

put.description: Records the tape colour of the roll in the printer and ends the prompt. ``colour`` null is both skip and clear. Send the ``width_mm`` the operator saw: a roll change detected meanwhile answers 409 ``roll-changed`` instead of colouring the new roll.

get.description: Returns the most recent status written by the background probe worker (SNMP for tape printers, IPP for page printers; page printers add ``kind``, ``printer_state``, reasons, markers, trays and ``jobs_ahead``). The response is served from ``printer_status_cache``. When no probe has completed yet ``online`` is ``null`` and ``note`` explains why. Reads the hub's cache only; never contacts the printer. Returns 404 when the printer is not registered.
get.summary: Return the latest cached printer status

get.description: Returns the width, display label and raw media text of the tape loaded in the printer, read from the status cache that the SNMP status producer writes. ``colour`` comes from the operator's roll record and is null until one exists. Answers 404 when there is no tape to report; see the 404 response.

404.description: No tape to report: the printer is unknown, has no cached status (``no cached status for printer ...``), is not polled (``Not polled``), its status is stale (``Status older than N s``, as in the status note), it is offline (``printer offline``: the hub cannot see a tape through a printer it cannot reach), or no tape is loaded (``no tape loaded in printer ...``). The body is ``{"detail": "<text>"}``.

get.summary: Get the tape loaded in a printer

post.description: Prints one test label on a tape printer (printer name, tape width, time, a QR to the printer's page in the hub) or one test page on a page printer (a frame on the printable area, name, tray, time, a QR). A tape printer is asked at submit time what tape is loaded, so the answer needs no polling; a page printer needs a fresh status.

409.description: `printer-disabled`, `printer-paused`, `printer-status-unknown` (page printer the hub does not poll), `printer-offline`, `no-tape-loaded` (tape printer), `media-unknown` (page printer) or `printer-unavailable`.

422.description: `tray-invalid`: a tray on a tape printer, or an unknown/disabled tray. `qr-payload-too-long`: the printer link does not fit the fixed QR code of the loaded tape (QL 62 mm).

post.summary: Print a test label (tape) or a test page (page printer)

post.description: Render a label using the LayoutEngine and return the result as a PNG image (no printer interaction, no job created).  Useful for UI preview and debugging.  Renders through the same engine call as a print job, so ``orientation`` and ``layout_preset`` give the exact image the job would print (an ``along`` image is the landscape band before the printer backend rotates it).  Returns 422 when ``data`` is missing fields required by ``content_type`` or the QR payload does not fit the fixed QR code (``qr_payload_too_long``).  Returns 409 when ``tape_mm`` is not a supported tape width or the orientation is not available for it.

post.description: Receives a Grocy webhook event for a product stock change and prints the product label through the print queue, like ``POST /api/v1/print``.  Requires the ``X-API-Key`` header — returns 503 when the key is not configured, 401 when the key is wrong, 422 when required payload fields are missing and 429 above the per-key rate limit.  Printer and lookup errors (no tape, printer disabled or offline, integration failed) are answered as by ``POST /api/v1/print`` (409/422/502/503); an unknown spool or product answers 404 ``app-lookup-not-found`` and an integration that is not configured 503 ``integration_not_configured`` (both in the problem-detail body shape). Nothing is queued.  On success returns 202 with the new job's UUID; the queue worker prints it.  One label is printed; a ``quantity`` in range is printed as the label's third line, in the hub's language, and never counts copies.
post.summary: Accept a Grocy product event and print its label

post.description: Grocy's label printer webhook (``LABEL_PRINTER_WEBHOOK``) for products, stock entries, chores, batteries and recipes.  **Authentication:** an API key with the ``print`` scope as the ``token`` query parameter (Grocy sends no headers) or the ``X-Label-Hub-Key`` header; a read key answers 403 ``insufficient_scope``, an admin key 403 ``token_scope_too_wide``, every other failure of the token 401 ``invalid_token``.  The key's printer restriction and rate limit apply.  The webhook is off until ``integrations.grocy.label.enabled`` is set.  The label type comes from the Grocycode; content type and printer come from the mapping of that type in Settings > Integrations > Grocy (a type without a printer uses the default target, and without one the first enabled tape printer).  The route answers 202 within 1.5 s with the job's UUID: printing runs afterwards, and a printer failure (offline, no tape) sets the job ``failed`` with the code ``POST /api/v1/print`` would answer.  A label that cannot be built (unreadable body, invalid Grocycode, name field of another type) also answers 202, with a ``failed`` job (``grocy_label_invalid``, ``grocy_label_mismatch``).

parameters.description: A Labelyard API key with the print scope (D24, ADR 0027). Read from a literal 'token=' parameter only; the X-Label-Hub-Key header wins when both are sent. The hub hides the value in its own logs
parameters.name: token

parameters.description: The same key as a header, for callers that can send headers
parameters.name: X-Label-Hub-Key

get.description: Returns 200 OK with a fixed shape. No authentication required. Used by Docker, Kubernetes, and reverse proxies to decide whether the backend is up. Has zero dependencies — does not touch the database, the printer queue, SNMP, or any integration. ``sse_active_subscribers`` reflects the current EventBus subscriber count; zero means no live SSE clients or the bus is uninitialised.

Deep readiness check: database connectivity, alembic migration state, printer wiring, SNMP probe recency, print-queue liveness, SSE subscriber capacity, and stuck render slots (`render_slots`: page renders past `LABELYARD_RENDER_TIMEOUT_S` whose thread still runs; fails when every slot is stuck, a hub restart frees them). Returns 200 with status in {ready, degraded} when all critical checks pass; 503 with status=not-ready when any critical check (database / alembic) fails.
